I need to understand how closed and open issue statuses are defined.

Open issues are neither done nor canceled. Sub-issue depth is capped at three levels. A move is invalid if the deepest descendant would exceed level three.

The deepest descendant of a moved subtree lands at the parent level plus one plus the subtree height. A move is invalid if that total exceeds three. Rooting an issue under a null parent resets it to level zero and always satisfies the depth limit. Cycles are forbidden: an issue cannot be placed under itself or under any descendant. The parent must be a live issue in the same project; another project or workspace returns NotFoundError, and an archived parent returns AlreadyArchivedError.

The same rules apply when creating an issue with a parent. An archived issue cannot be moved and returns AlreadyArchivedError. The actor needs issue:update permission on the issue being moved, plus issue:read for listing and rollup. Operations outside the actor's workspace return TenantScopeError, and missing issues return NotFoundError. A successful move or removal of the parent triggers an issue.updated announcement with parentId in changedFields.

The issue.updated announcement will only fire when the parent actually changes, matching the status-change pattern. If the requested parent is already stored, no event is emitted.

Listing returns direct sub-issues oldest first, by creation time and then issue number, excluding archived ones. Roll-up counts every non-archived descendant at any depth: total, open, and closed. Closed means done or canceled; open means neither. Archiving an issue archives every live descendant at any depth, but already archived issues remain untouched. Each newly archived issue receives exactly one issue.archived event. Archiving a sub-issue never affects its parent.

When a sub-issue closes or is archived while open, and its direct parent is left with no remaining open issues below it at any depth, the parent's assignee receives a single `sub_issues_completed` notification. This follows standard fan-out rules including recipient preferences, and the actor who made the change is excluded. No notification is sent if the parent has no assignee or is already archived.

The completion notification is not sent when a sub-issue is merely moved or reopened. It only fires when the sub-issue actually closes or is archived while open. The parent must have zero open issues at any depth below it for the notification to trigger. Reopening and closing a sub-issue again will notify the assignee again. Only the direct parent is considered, and the notice targets the direct parent of the issue being archived or closed.

Archiving a parent first archives its open children. The completion notification must not fire for those children because their direct parent is already archived.

When archiving a parent, the completion notification should fire for that parent's direct parent if it is left with no open descendants. For example, if grandparent GP has open sub-issue P which has open sub-issue C, archiving P archives both P and C. P is now archived so no notice fires for it. GP remains live and may be notified once if no other open issues below it remain.

The notification handler must listen for both issue.archived and issue.status_changed events. The implementation plan is to add a depth constant, define an IssueHierarchyError, create an IssueRollup type, and build a setIssueParentSchema. Repository helpers will include setParent, list children by parent, and fetch all issues in a project. SQLite recursive CTEs via Drizzle sql support the tree walks.

I will load every issue in the project into memory to validate depth and cycles, since the dataset is small. I can also walk upward from the parent to compute its level, or walk downward for descendant counts.

A parent already at level three cannot accept children, since that would push the child to level four. The cycle check walks upward from the new parent and stops if it reaches the issue being moved. I am also weighing whether archived descendants count toward the depth limit when judging a move.

Archived descendants still carry parent links and would land at a level, so they count toward the depth limit when judging a move. The shallow-tree rule governs placement, not archived state.

Parent validation will run in `createIssue` before insertion and in `setIssueParent`. If the parent is refused, the issue is not created and no event is emitted. A null parent on creation skips all checks. A parent from another organization returns `NotFoundError` through `findIssueById`.

The codebase typically checks organization scope first, then finds the issue, then verifies permissions, and finally asserts it is not archived. This order matters for tests.

The parent lookup will first confirm the issue belongs to the same project, then check archive status, and only after both passes will it evaluate cycles and depth.
